title: Chain of Responsibility

act2.summary: a warmup check inserted in the middle of the order, and the whole order reversed for one telescope (weather first)

solutions.title: Six checks as linked rule objects, ordered per telescope
solutions.tradeoff: Inserting or reordering a check is a change to one function (the chain builder) instead of a change to the order of six if-statements in a row. The price: to know what a single check does, or whether a telescope even runs it, you can no longer just read one function top to bottom - you have to also open the chain builder to find out which rules apply and in what order.

reviewFocus: Does inserting InstrumentWarmupRule touch any of the five existing rule classes, or only chain.ts and the new rule's own file?
Does Ridgeline's reordered chain reuse the same five rule instances/classes as every other telescope, or does it duplicate any check logic?

Is telescope.name === "Ridgeline" an honest way to special-case one telescope, or does it deserve a real field on Telescope (e.g. checkOrder) instead - and does the walkthrough take a position on that?
Does BaseRule's handle() still work correctly if a rule chain is built with only one rule in it (no setNext call at all)?
Is the walkthrough honest about where this act 2 wins (lines) and where it does not (hunks, where the no-pattern route's one big duplicated block actually lands in fewer hunks)?
